To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the majority of research articles in special education practitioner journals do not translate intervention research findings to classroom practice for students with mild disabilities.

(a) the majority of articles published in practitioner journals do not translate intervention research findings to teachers, (b) articles that did translate findings were most likely to target academics, (c) articles were most likely to translate findings to practice in elementary grades and least likely to translate findings for secondary teachers, and (d) the number of articles translated to practice was low for all types of disabilities.

(a) there is a lack of research that translates intervention research to practice in special education journals; (b) the majority of articles in special education journals that translate intervention research to practice are focused on academics, with few articles focused on social-emotional or behavioral interventions; and (c) articles that translate intervention research for teachers who work specifically with students with mild disability are rare.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the translation of evidence-based practices for teachers of students with disabilities.
the extent to which intervention research for students with mild disabilities is translated to practice in special education practitioner journals.
the question, "How do we translate research to practice?" and our findings suggest that the field is not yet doing a very good job.

there is a need for more research-to-practice articles that target the specific needs of students with mild disabilities and that these articles should be written in a way that is easy for classroom teachers to understand.
the current research is not being translated to practice in a manner that will help teachers who work with A-L1 students.
research on effective interventions for students with mild disabilities is not being translated to practice.

the majority of research articles published in practitioner journals do not address the needs of teachers who work with the largest proportion of students with disabilities. (author abstract)
